findings.text: At <=96 nodes/axis the v009 docstring says requests, inputs and reports are byte-identical to c2v008. TESTED: the dry-run plan and every simulated input are byte-identical. The DRYRUN_REPORT differs in 4 leaves: driver_sha256, static_pins and transitive_pins.files gain the prep_v009 entry, and transitive_pins.verified_files rises by 1. Harmless, since it is one extra verified pin. Suggested wording: "plan and inputs byte-identical; reports additionally list the prep v009 pin".

The C5/C6 N8_M32 specs differ from C4R3 in more than grid, k_max and route_a. TESTED leaf diff: (1) admit.route_a, admit.reference and admit.body are removed, so route A, reference and body are computed fresh at G5/G6, as they must be; (2) the composite grid is G5 or G6; (3) numerics.route_a gains column_workers 8, which selects the parallel route A where C4R3 ran serial, and max_iterations 32; (4) the label. This matches the spec label "derived from C4R3 3ea94efe by admit/grid/route_a/label only". Brackets equal the D7 R3 block bitwise.

In both route-A solvers (serial 44d9c23c and parallel aed4dd59), max_iterations is validated (int >= 1), recorded in the checkpoint identity controls, and used only as the loop bound (for iteration in range(start_iteration, max_iterations)). It therefore enters the route-A identity sha: an admitted rerun of a C5/C6 prefix must carry the same value, which the driver states route_a_custody enforces.
